candidate_relations.reason: Thrombotic stroke from chronic left ICA occlusion is an incompatible mechanism versus primary CNS angiitis, even though ICA occlusion was present.
Cardioembolic stroke from atrial fibrillation is a competing embolic cause and does not capture PACNS; CSF had mild pleocytosis.
Hypertensive vasculopathy is an incompatible chronic small-vessel cause versus PACNS, and ambulatory blood pressure was normal.
Infective endocarditis with embolism is a different septic embolic disease; cultures were negative.
Malignant orbital lymphoma with CNS infiltration is a different neoplastic explanation for the orbital lesions; neoplasm was excluded by consultants.
Cancer-associated stroke is a different paraneoplastic/thrombotic mechanism not established here.
The truncated sarcoidosis label is a discounted granulomatous differential, not PACNS.
Ischemic stroke is the presenting infarct, not primary angiitis of the CNS.
Stroke is a manifestation of PACNS rather than the vasculitic diagnosis.
Cerebral amyloid angiopathy is a different microangiopathy and typically hemorrhagic, unlike this large-artery infarct.
Intracerebral hemorrhage conflicts with documented ischemic MCA infarction.
Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis is a different embolic source not demonstrated.
Aortic stenosis is a documented valve lesion, not PACNS.
Cardioembolic stroke due to severe aortic stenosis asserts an incompatible embolic mechanism versus PACNS.
The orbital-lymphoma exclusion fragment is not PACNS and concerns a different orbital mass interpretation.
Acute ischemic stroke describes the MCA infarct without the PACNS etiology.
Moyamoya disease is a different steno-occlusive syndrome not described angiographically.
Giant cell arteritis is a related large-vessel vasculitis but systemic vasculitis was excluded, conflicting with PACNS.
Severe aortic stenosis is comorbidity, not primary CNS angiitis.
Aortic stenosis with embolic stroke again attributes the infarct to valve disease rather than PACNS.

case_quality_flags: No complete_equivalent candidate names primary angiitis of the CNS; competing cardioembolic explanations (AF, ICA occlusion, aortic stenosis) are prominent in the record.
